brief: Acts as a local OpenID Connect identity provider with a real signing key, so sign-in is developed without a provider account.
detail: It is not a stub that answers true. It holds an ES256 key pair, publishes the public half as a key set and a discovery document, and signs every token in the engine, so the relying party, stzOidcClient, runs its genuine signature check against a genuine key set. It also mints deliberately bad tokens, expired, forged, or with another audience, issuer or nonce, through IssueIdTokenXT, so the refusals can be tested, which a real provider will not do on request. The key comes from the engine's generator or from a seed for a reproducible suite, and is a sandbox key, never a real one. Token claims are joined into the JSON without escaping, so it must not be fed untrusted values.
receiver:
o1 = new stzOidcSandbox("https://idp.local", "my-app")
o2 = new stzOidcClient("https://idp.local", "my-app")
